purpose: Row-shape expectation: declare what a data row looks like so rows that do not qualify escalate. Third separate measurement; K and the C3-fix replay stand as measured.
correction_to_the_record: results/RESULT_c3fix.md speculated a row-shape rule 'would plausibly recover C13 and C8 both'. Working it through before building shows only C13 is recoverable this way: a subtotal row has exactly the shape of a data row and differs only in meaning. The corrected prediction is frozen here.

format_v12.key: data_row_shape, one optional key per data-sheet entry
format_v12.security_note: Both constraints are TYPE-LEVEL: they ask what KIND of value sits in a cell, never what it says. No patterns, no regex, no value lists -- a predicate language over untrusted cell content is an expression language through the back door.
format_v12.cost: v1.2 makes the validator read data-row CONTENT, where v1/v1.1 read structure plus the header row. Bounded deliberately: it learns only blank/numeric/neither per cell and never branches on what a cell says, so a malicious workbook can cause an ESCALATION and nothing else. Escalation is the safe direction, so the widened surface buys detection without buying authority.
